title: Regression: unable to eagerly fetch related entity through polymorphic join

labels.name: loader options
labels.description: ORM options like joinedload(), load_only(), these are complicated and have a lot of issues

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: inheritance
labels.description: issues to do wtih ORM inheritance, a particularly tricky area

body:
When trying to configure an eager join on an entity related to a polymorphic subclass of a related entity, the leaf related entity is not eagerly fetched.

Between release 1.3.0b2 and 1.3.0b3, this behavior changed. The likely commit that introduced this behavior change is 95c371f1d3007071a32fad1d67329e6f9d56931b, related to #4469.

Example:

``` python
from sqlalchemy import (
    Column,
    ForeignKey,
    Integer,
    MetaData,
    String,
    create_engine
)
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import (
    backref,
    joinedload,
    relationship,
    scoped_session,
    sessionmaker,
    with_polymorphic,
)


Base = declarative_base()


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class Foo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foos"
    __mapper_args__ = {"polymorphic_on": "type"}

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    type = Column(String, nullable=False)
    owner_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"))
    owner = relationship("User", backref=backref("foos"), cascade="all")


class SubFoo(Foo):
    __tablename__ = "foos_sub"
    __mapper_args__ = {"polymorphic_identity": "SUB"}

    id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("foos.id"), primary_key=True)
    baz = Column(Integer)
    bar_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("bars.id"))
    bar = relationship("Bar")


class Bar(Base):
    __tablename__ = "bars"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    fred_id = Column(
        Integer,
        ForeignKey("freds.id"),
        nullable=False
    )
    fred = relationship("Fred")


class Fred(Base):
    __tablename__ = "freds"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


engine = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
metadata = MetaData()
with engine.begin() as connection:
    metadata = Base.metadata
    metadata.create_all(connection)

session = scoped_session(sessionmaker(bind=engine))

# Setup some related entities
user = User()
fred = Fred()
bar = Bar(fred=fred)
rectangle = SubFoo(owner=user, baz=10, bar=bar)
session.add_all([user, fred, bar, rectangle])
session.commit()
session.remove()

foo_polymorphic = with_polymorphic(Foo, "*", aliased=True)

foo_load = joinedload(User.foos.of_type(foo_polymorphic))
query = session.query(User).options(
    foo_load.joinedload(foo_polymorphic.SubFoo.bar).joinedload(Bar.fred)
)
print("##########begin")
user = query.one()
user.foos[0].bar
print("##########accessing bar's fred")
# We expect this entity to have been eagerly loaded.
user.foos[0].bar.fred
print("##########end")
```

Tail output with version "1.3.0b2":

```
##########begin
2020-01-06 23:19:09,339 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine BEGIN (implicit)
2020-01-06 23:19:09,342 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine SELECT users.id AS users_id, anon_1.foos_id AS anon_1_foos_id, anon_1.foos_type AS anon_1_foos_type, anon_1.foos_owner_id AS anon_1_foos_owner_id, freds_1.id AS freds_1_id, bars_1.id AS bars_1_id, bars_1.fred_id AS bars_1_fred_id, anon_1.foos_sub_id AS anon_1_foos_sub_id, anon_1.foos_sub_baz
AS anon_1_foos_sub_baz, anon_1.foos_sub_bar_id AS anon_1_foos_sub_bar_id
FROM users LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT foos.id AS foos_id, foos.type AS foos_type, foos.owner_id AS foos_owner_id, foos_sub.id AS foos_sub_id, foos_sub.baz AS foos_sub_baz, foos_sub.bar_id AS foos_sub_bar_id
FROM foos LEFT OUTER JOIN foos_sub ON foos.id = foos_sub.id) AS anon_1 ON users.id = anon_1.foos_owner_id LEFT OUTER JOIN bars AS bars_1 ON bars_1.id = anon_1.foos_sub_bar_id LEFT OUTER JOIN freds AS freds_1 ON freds_1.id = bars_1.fred_id
2020-01-06 23:19:09,342 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine ()
##########accessing bar's fred
##########end
```

Tail output with version "1.3.0b3":

```
##########begin
2020-01-06 23:21:20,252 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine BEGIN (implicit)
2020-01-06 23:21:20,256 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine SELECT users.id AS users_id, anon_1.foos_id AS anon_1_foos_id, anon_1.foos_type AS anon_1_foos_type, anon_1.foos_owner_id AS anon_1_foos_owner_id, bars_1.id AS bars_1_id, bars_1.fred_id AS bars_1_fred_id, anon_1.foos_sub_id AS anon_1_foos_sub_id, anon_1.foos_sub_baz AS anon_1_foos_sub_baz, anon_1.foos_sub_bar_id AS anon_1_foos_sub_bar_id 
FROM users LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT foos.id AS foos_id, foos.type AS foos_type, foos.owner_id AS foos_owner_id, foos_sub.id AS foos_sub_id, foos_sub.baz AS foos_sub_baz, foos_sub.bar_id AS foos_sub_bar_id 
FROM foos LEFT OUTER JOIN foos_sub ON foos.id = foos_sub.id) AS anon_1 ON users.id = anon_1.foos_owner_id LEFT OUTER JOIN bars AS bars_1 ON bars_1.id = anon_1.foos_sub_bar_id
2020-01-06 23:21:20,256 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine ()
##########accessing bar's fred
2020-01-06 23:21:20,262 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine SELECT freds.id AS freds_id 
FROM freds 
WHERE freds.id = ?
2020-01-06 23:21:20,262 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine (1,)
##########end
```

Note the parent `User` record is required to reproduce the bug. For example, querying directly for the polymorphic `Foo` classes works as expected.

``` python
foo_polymorphic = with_polymorphic(Foo, "*")
query = session.query(foo_polymorphic).options(
    joinedload(foo_polymorphic.SubFoo.bar).joinedload(Bar.fred)
)
sub_foo = query.one()
sub_foo.bar
sub_foo.bar.fred
# ^ emits a single query
```
